Thanks Alicia — great to meet you today. Below is a tight post-call summary and a proposed evaluation guardrail set so we can move directly to scheduling a kickoff.

Recap of ask
- Sandbox run to validate latency & token economics against your 50k-turn workload.
- Deliverables: time-series latency/throughput graphs, per-call token cost, and quality checks against your annotation set.

Proposed success criteria (draft)
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 320ms (end-to-end server-side generation for 1–3 token outputs typical for short responses); for longer multi-turn flows we target p50 < 250ms, p95 < 600ms.
- Throughput: sustain 250 concurrent small-turn QPS with 95% request success (no retries) during a 1-hour stress window.
- Cost: average generation cost <= $0.0018 / 1k tokens (measured across replay; we will report token breakdown).
- Quality: intent-match >= 88% on your labeled set; hallucination incidents <= 3% of evaluated queries (random 200-sample audit).

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Day 0: kickoff and sandbox credential handoff (Redwood provides ephemeral sandbox key + dashboard).
- Day 1–3: ingest sample workload, smoke validation, baseline run (small volume).
- Week 1: scaled replay to reach target concurrency and gather metrics.
- Week 2–3: run stability window and quality sampling; weekly readout.
- Week 4: final results, recommendations (model variant, quantization, batching config).

Ownership
- AE / primary contact: Kimberly Park (owner for cadence, SOW).
- Solutions engineer / test lead: Ben Carter (setup, metrics instrumentation).
- Infra / capacity lead: Marcus Lin (throughput, autoscale knobs).

Next steps
1) Confirm sandbox start window (you suggested next week).
2) Alicia: share the full replay file (we have the sample) and any evaluation labels you want included.
3) Redwood: send the short SLA/proposal deck + metrics template (attached) and a calendar invite for kickoff.

Attachments: redwood-trial-sla-proposal.pdf, trial-metrics-template.xlsx

Links: HubSpot record + Drive folder above.

Thanks — Kim

Quick tech note — adding a couple practical constraints we should surface to Lumos before kickoff:
1) Model variant: for their throughput profile I recommend starting on the 'redwood-medium-q3' quantized variant (best tradeoff for cost/latency). We can flip to a larger non-quantized model for quality checks if the quality audit drops below 88%.
2) KV caching and prompt prefix: suggest enabling prefix caching for multi-turn flows to reduce p95 by ~15–25% on longer conversations; we should include a short test that toggles cache on/off.
3) Throughput tuning: the 250-concurrent target is achievable if we provision a small dedicated burst pool for the 1-hour stress window — Marcus, can you confirm a quick capacity reservation?

I updated the metrics template with two columns: (a) with-cache and (b) without-cache performance. Also flagged a small instrumentation ask: please ensure Lumos shares a canonical mapping for "system" vs "assistant" tokens in their replay so cost attribution is accurate.

—Ben
